newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ trade balance trend continues improving in Nov.
newsitem.headline: NZ trade balance trend continues improving in Nov.

text.p: The trend in New Zealand's merchandise trade balance continued to improve in November, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
It said the trade balance trend had been improving since a low point in February, as the exports trend fell at a slower rate than the imports trend.

The trend in exports continued to decline, falling by an average 0.2 percent per month from a high point in July. The imports trend has shown a deterioration from a high point in March, averaging a monthly fall of 0.4 percent over that time.
The trade deficit in November was NZ$92 million, compared with a deficit of $285 million in November 1995.

Unadjusted exports for November were valued at NZ$1.75 billion, up 1.7 percent on a year ago. Exports of dairy produce, meat, wood and wood articles accounted for 38 percent of total exports in the month.
The unadjusted value of imports for November was NZ$1.84 billion, down 8.2 percent from November 1995. Mechanical machinery and aircraft contributed to the decrease.
Unadjusted exports for the year ended November were NZ$21.01 billion, down 0.1 percent from the previous year. Imports over the same period rose 0.9 percent to $21.41 billion.
A trade deficit of $399 million was recorded for the November year, against a $172 million deficit in the November 1995 year.

If large, irregular items such as ships and aircraft were excluded, the trade deficit for the year would have been $294 million, while the November 1995 year trade balance would have been a $138 million surplus.
